title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels
abstract: arXiv:2611.08046v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Nowadays, large language models produce text at scale, and much of it is redistributed across platforms. A moderator who finds a suspicious comment, post or article may want to know which platform generated it and for which account. In this paper we study attribution over the channel through which such text actually travels, copy-paste, which discards document metadata but keeps Unicode code points. We present KeHoSu, which turns the confusable characters of homoglyph attacks into a keyed attribution channel: the variant chosen for each carrier letter encodes one bit of an identifier made of a platform field, a user field and a truncated authentication tag. Moreover, given that reshared text is often quoted in fragments, and the placement therefore keeps no positional state, we show that KeHoSu is invariant to sentence reordering up to a constant boundary layer and depends on a partial quotation only through the retained length. translated_title: KeHoSu：面向复制粘贴渠道认证文本溯源的密钥同形字替换
translated_abstract: 如今，大型语言模型大规模生成文本，其中许多文本在各平台间被重新分发。当版主发现可疑的评论、帖子或文章时，可能想知道它是由哪个平台生成、属于哪个账户。本文研究了此类文本实际传播的渠道——复制粘贴——上的归属问题：该渠道会丢弃文档元数据，但保留Unicode码点。我们提出了KeHoSu，它将同形字攻击中的易混淆字符转变为带密钥的归属信道：为每个载体字母选择的字符变体编码了标识符中的一个比特，该标识符由平台字段、用户字段和截断的认证标签组成。此外，鉴于转发文本常以片段形式被引用，其排版不保留位置状态，我们证明KeHoSu对句子重排具有不变性（至多存在一个恒定的边界层），且对部分引用的依赖仅通过所保留的长度体现。
tldr: 提出KeHoSu方法，将同形字攻击中的易混淆字符转化为带密钥的归属信道，通过Unicode字符变体在文本中嵌入平台、用户与认证标签信息，实现复制粘贴渠道下的文本溯源，并对句子重排和部分引用保持鲁棒。
